title: Frugal batcher and quant-profile orchestrator: adaptive defaults + unit-econ simulator
author: Priya Nair
release_notes: Introduces Frugal Batcher adaptive defaults, Quant-Profile Orchestrator, and a Unit Economics simulator. Defaults are non-breaking and gated behind feature flag. Improves per-token cost by ~12% on internal benchmarks (see notes).
description:
Motivation: Many customers see large variance in serving unit economics because static batching/cache/quantization defaults are a poor fit for real traffic patterns. This PR introduces two cooperating subsystems: Frugal Batcher (per-route adaptive batching + cache policy defaults) and Quant-Profile Orchestrator (model-aware quantization recommendations and safe fallbacks). Also adds a lightweight Unit Economics simulator to validate suggestions before rollout. This change is behind the feature flag 'cost_opt_v2' and is opt-in by default.

What this PR changes (high level):
- Runtime: new frugal-batcher scheduler plug-in that collects per-route sequence-length histograms, idle-latency signals, and backpressure to pick batching windows and target batch sizes. Adds prefix-aware KV-cache policy hints emitted as route metadata.
- Model tooling: quant-profile-orchestrator service that computes a small candidate set of quantization profiles (int8/4-bit variants, per-layer heuristics) and attaches stability metadata (eval delta on synthetic prompt set).
- Console/API: exposes suggested defaults in the Console (route settings panel) and a CLI evaluation mode (redwood ctl cost-simulate) that runs the Unit Economics simulator locally against a sample workload.
- Telemetry and safety: new tracing/span tags and metrics (batcher.chosen_window_ms, quant.orchestrator.confidence, ue.simulated_cost_delta) plus a regression guard that prevents auto-application of profiles with >0.5% quality delta on the canonical prompt set.

Why this is safe: defaults are suggestions — no automatic model re-quantization is performed unless explicitly approved by an operator. Orchestrator runs offline evaluation and stores stability metadata; runtime will only reference profiles marked 'runtime-safe' by the operator. All traffic-affecting behavior is behind the feature flag and a rollout plan in the Console.

Testing done:
- Unit tests for scheduling heuristics and quant-profile scoring logic (new test modules: test_frugal_batcher.py, test_quant_orchestrator.py)
- Integration: end-to-end canary on staging with synthetic workload (see CI job 'canary/cost-opt'). Warm runs showed 9–15% cost delta improvement depending on model family and sequence-length distribution.
- Safety: ran regression evals against the household canonical prompt-set, verified quality deltas below 0.3% on recommended profiles.

Checklist: 
- [x] Design doc linked in the PR (Linear ENG-3456)
- [x] Unit tests added and passing
- [x] Integration canary job configured
- [x] Console UI changes behind feature toggle
- [x] Telemetry and dashboards updated
- [x] Release notes drafted

How to try locally: 
1) Enable feature flag: export REDWOOD_FEATURE_FLAGS="cost_opt_v2=true"
2) Build: make dev-runtime
3) Start the frugal-batcher in dev mode: services/frugal-batcher/bin/start --dev
4) Run simulator: redwood ctl cost-simulate --route /chat --sample-file testdata/sample_trace.json

Related: ENG-3456 (design), ENG-3521 (quant orchestration prototype).

Notes for reviewers: Pay attention to the scheduler heuristics (frugal_batcher/scheduler.py) and the confidence scoring in quant_orchestrator/scorer.py; both include comments with tunable constants. The approach prioritizes low-latency SLOs over pure cost savings and exposes the tradeoffs in the Console UI.

Merge plan: squash merge; feature remains gated. Follow rollout playbook in docs/runbooks/cost-opt-rollout.md.
